public_rationale: Trend Micro's June 5, 2025 report falls within the January 1–August 17, 2025 observation window. It reports mostly hallucination-free foundation-model outputs across 100 web-development tasks, with occasional fabricated package names on complex prompts [e1]. Agents were tested on the ten tasks with the highest foundation-model hallucination rates; reasoning and search approximately halved hallucinations, while live validation filtered out most remaining errors but left some fabricated names [e1]. These results support a practical risk from invented dependencies when coding with LLMs, while showing that safeguards reduce that risk [e1]. They do not establish that the problem is inherent or unavoidable [e1].
limitations: The June 5 report does not give exact experiment dates, limiting certainty that all measurements occurred within the observation window [e1].
The selected agent tasks do not establish the average developer's risk or representative production failure rates [e1].
Fabricated package names do not establish actual malware infections, failure in every generated program, or architectural inevitability [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs have apparently inherent reliability problems, and code written with them contains hallucinations, making LLM coding risky.
conditions: when writing code with an LLM

statement.excerpt: Gary has written here endlessly about the troubles with reliability, apparently inherent, in LLMs. If you write code with an LLM, you are asking for trouble; the kind of garden-variety hallucinations that Gary has described in, for example, biographies, have parallels in LLM-generated code.

from_speaker: troubles with reliability, apparently inherent, in LLMs

hallucinations ... have parallels in LLM-generated code
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that LLM-generated code has recurring fabricated dependencies or other invented references that create practical reliability risks.
Apparently inherent expresses a tentative explanation. It is not treated as a firm claim that every possible future system must fail.
The statement describes technology available at publication. With no standard reporting quarter for this subject, the observation window is the current calendar year through 2025-08-17.
Asking for trouble means exposure to a real risk, not that every generated program fails.
criteria.support_condition: Systematic evaluations in the observation period find recurring hallucinated code dependencies or references, with credible consequences for execution or security.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evaluations find that the claimed hallucinations are absent or practically negligible across ordinary code-generation tasks.
